titulo: Understanding Others and Expressing Personal Viewpoints
titulo_es: Entender a otros y expresar puntos de vista
estandares: Comprendo y expreso opiniones sobre costumbres y actividades cotidianas. Distingo entre lo habitual y lo temporal al describir la vida propia y la de otras culturas.
competencias: Contrastar presente simple y presente continuo en contextos reales; usar adverbios y expresiones de frecuencia; saludar y despedirse según el registro; describir costumbres y tradiciones y opinar sobre ellas.
componentes: Pensamiento crítico, comunicación, colaboración y creatividad.

proyecto.descripcion_es: En grupos, los estudiantes investigan una tradición de otro país y la presentan comparándola con una costumbre colombiana, usando presente simple para lo habitual y presente continuo para lo que está cambiando hoy.
proyecto.descripcion_en: In groups, students research a tradition from another country and present it comparing it with a Colombian custom, using the simple present for what is habitual and the present continuous for what is changing today.

lecciones.content_es:
Lo permanente y lo temporal

  • Presente simple: rutinas, hechos, verdades generales. Water boils at 100 °C.
  • Presente continuo: acción de ahora, situación temporal o tendencia en curso. She is living with her aunt this year.

Usos menos obvios del continuo

  • Cambios en desarrollo: The climate is getting warmer.
  • Planes ya concretados: We are traveling to Cali on Friday.
  • Quejas con always: He's always interrupting me!

Verbos de estado

know, believe, understand, want, need, own, seem, belong, prefer normalmente no van en continuo. Pero algunos cambian de significado: I think it's true (opinión) vs. I'm thinking about it (proceso mental).
lecciones.content_en:
Permanent and temporary

  • Present simple: routines, facts, general truths. Water boils at 100 °C.
  • Present continuous: an action right now, a temporary situation or an ongoing trend. She is living with her aunt this year.

Less obvious uses of the continuous

  • Developing changes: The climate is getting warmer.
  • Fixed plans: We are traveling to Cali on Friday.
  • Complaints with always: He's always interrupting me!

State verbs

know, believe, understand, want, need, own, seem, belong, prefer normally do not take the continuous. Some change meaning: I think it's true (opinion) vs. I'm thinking about it (mental process).

lecciones.content_es:
La escala completa

always · almost always · usually · often / frequently · sometimes · occasionally · hardly ever / rarely · never.

Posición

  • Antes del verbo principal: I usually walk to school.
  • Después de to be: He is rarely late.
  • Entre auxiliar y verbo: She has never been abroad.

Expresiones que van al final

every day, once a week, twice a month, from time to time, most of the time, on weekends.

Cuidado con los negativos

never, rarely y hardly ever ya son negativos: no se combinan con don't. I hardly ever eat fast food, no I don't hardly ever eat.
lecciones.content_en:
The full scale

always · almost always · usually · often / frequently · sometimes · occasionally · hardly ever / rarely · never.

Position

  • Before the main verb: I usually walk to school.
  • After to be: He is rarely late.
  • Between auxiliary and verb: She has never been abroad.

Expressions that go at the end

every day, once a week, twice a month, from time to time, most of the time, on weekends.

Careful with negatives

never, rarely and hardly ever are already negative: they are not combined with don't.

lecciones.t: Saludos y despedidas según el registro
lecciones.content_es:
Formal

Good morning, Mr. Ruiz. · How do you do? · It's a pleasure to meet you. · I look forward to hearing from you. · Have a good day.

Informal

Hi! · Hey, what's up? · How's it going? · What have you been up to? · See you! · Take care! · Catch you later.

Responder

  • How are you? — I'm doing great, thanks. And yourself?
  • What's up? — Not much. You?

Elegir el registro

Con profesores, adultos desconocidos y correos escolares: formal. Con compañeros y amigos: informal. How do you do? solo se usa la primera vez y en contextos muy formales.
lecciones.content_en:
Formal

Good morning, Mr. Ruiz. · How do you do? · It's a pleasure to meet you. · I look forward to hearing from you. · Have a good day.

Informal

Hi! · Hey, what's up? · How's it going? · What have you been up to? · See you! · Take care! · Catch you later.

Answering

  • How are you? — I'm doing great, thanks. And yourself?
  • What's up? — Not much. You?

Choosing the register

With teachers, unknown adults and school emails: formal. With classmates and friends: informal. How do you do? is only used the first time and in very formal contexts.

lecciones.t_en: Customs and traditions around the world
lecciones.content_es:
Vocabulario clave

custom (costumbre), tradition, celebration, festival, holiday (día festivo), ceremony, ritual, heritage (patrimonio), ancestors (antepasados), folklore, costume (traje típico), parade (desfile).

Cómo describirlas

  • In Japan, people take off their shoes before entering a house.
  • It is a tradition to eat twelve grapes at midnight.
  • People usually gather to celebrate.

Falso amigo

costume es traje o disfraz, no costumbre. Costumbre es custom.

Opinar

I find it fascinating. · It seems strange to me at first, but it makes sense. · In my culture we do it differently.
lecciones.content_en:
Key vocabulary

custom, tradition, celebration, festival, holiday, ceremony, ritual, heritage, ancestors, folklore, costume, parade.

How to describe them

  • In Japan, people take off their shoes before entering a house.
  • It is a tradition to eat twelve grapes at midnight.
  • People usually gather to celebrate.

False friend

costume is an outfit or a disguise, not a habit. A habit or usage is a custom.

Giving an opinion

I find it fascinating. · It seems strange to me at first, but it makes sense. · In my culture we do it differently.

lecciones.content_es:
Actividades cotidianas

hang out with friends (pasar el rato), chat online, scroll through social media, work out (entrenar), volunteer (ser voluntario), help out at home, practice an instrument, attend classes.

Hablar de hábitos

  • I tend to study at night. (tiendo a)
  • I'm used to waking up early. (estoy acostumbrado a)
  • I've picked up the habit of reading before bed.

Dar tu punto de vista

In my opinion… · I believe that… · From my point of view… · It seems to me that… · I'd say that…

Para matizar: I'm not sure, but… · It depends on… · To some extent…

repaso.resumen_es:
Lo esencial del periodo

La decisión central es simple o continuo: lo permanente y habitual va en presente simple; lo temporal, lo que está en curso o en cambio va en presente continuo. Los adverbios de frecuencia matizan el simple.

Puntos gramaticales

  • Verbos de estado (know, want, belong) no admiten forma continua.
  • think, have y see cambian de significado en continuo.
  • El adverbio va antes del verbo principal, después de to be y entre auxiliar y participio.
  • never, rarely y hardly ever ya son negativos.

Vocabulario

Saludos formales e informales, instrucciones de clase en imperativo, costumbres y tradiciones (custom ≠ costume) y fórmulas para dar opiniones.
repaso.resumen_en:
The core of the term

The central decision is simple or continuous: what is permanent and habitual goes in the present simple; what is temporary, ongoing or changing goes in the present continuous. Frequency adverbs fine-tune the simple.

Grammar points

  • State verbs (know, want, belong) have no continuous form.
  • think, have and see change meaning in the continuous.
  • The adverb goes before the main verb, after to be, and between auxiliary and participle.
  • never, rarely and hardly ever are already negative.

Vocabulary

Formal and informal greetings, classroom instructions in the imperative, customs and traditions (custom ≠ costume) and formulas for giving opinions.
puntos_clave: Permanente → simple; temporal o en curso → continuo.
Permanent → simple; temporary or ongoing → continuous.
I know, no I am knowing.
I know, not I am knowing.
is always + -ing expresa queja, no rutina.
is always + -ing expresses a complaint, not a routine.
hardly ever ya es negativo: no lleva don't.
hardly ever is already negative: it takes no don't.
look forward to y be used to llevan gerundio.
look forward to and be used to take a gerund.
custom = costumbre; costume = traje o disfraz.
